newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Barak starts campaign to be premier.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Barak starts campaign to be premier.

text.p: Ex-army chief Ehud Barak launched a campaign on Monday to succeed Shimon Peres as head of the opposition Labour Party and become Israeli prime minister in elections due in four years.
"I have decided to run for the prime ministership in the year 2000...and to that end, to run for the leadership of the Labour Party," Barak, 54, told a news conference.
Long touted as a future prime minister, the ambitious and confident Barak, like his slain mentor Yitzhak Rabin, combines an impressive military record with a blunt demeanor popular among Israelis.

Barak said he was ready to face present party chairman Peres in party elections for the Labour Party leadership in June, 1997. Peres, who became prime minister on Rabin's assassination but was defeated in May's Israeli election, has not said if he wants to stay party leader.
"I have made my decision, and I will run in any case -- period," said Barak, a former commando who retired from the military in January, 1995 after 35 years of service.

Benjamin Netanyahu, 47, defeated Peres in May in a campaign that stressed the Likud leader's own record as a commando officer. Peres, although he held the defence ministry's most senior posts, never served in the army.

"I believe that the Labour party will return to power in the next election, and I believe in my power to bring about security, peace, and prosperity for Israel, while preserving the unity of the people," Barak said.
He said he would return Labour to "its natural place in the centre of the political map, as a party of the centre," in apparent contrast to Peres, who is considered a political dove.
The 73-year-old Peres, who won the Nobel Peace prize for forging the 1993 Israeli-Palestinian peace agreement with PLO leader Yasser Arafat, has maintained he will continue "battling for peace".
But Peres, the perennial loser of Israeli politics who has been defeated five times as Labour candidate for prime minister, would not say if he would seek to remain party chairman.
The former prime minister, visiting New York, said of the Barak candidacy: "He can submit it, that's just fine."
In an interview with Israel Radio, Peres declined to say if he would challenge Barak and two other ex-ministers expected to vie for his job, dove Haim Ramon and centrist Ephraim Sneh.
As army chief Barak oversaw the first handover of occupied land to the Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank town of Jericho under the 1993 peace deal Peres negotiated with the PLO.
Rabin named him interior minister in July, 1995. After Rabin's assassination last November, interim prime minister Peres chose Barak to take over his vacated post as foreign minister.
